Consider the vector $v$ shown above. Find the vector $Av$ given that 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4} & \frac{\sqrt{2}}{4} \\ -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4} & -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}\end{aligned}].
$$
worked_solution:
Notice that $A$ is a rotation-scaling matrix. So, we need to find its scale factor and the angle of rotation.

We can find the scale factor using the following formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\sqrt{det(A)} \\  & =\sqrt{{(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4})}^{2}+{(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can represent $A$ as a product of a rotation and a scaling matrix, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} & \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\ -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} & -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} & \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\ -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} & -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}r & 0 \\ 0 & r\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & -\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we obtain that

$$
{\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta =-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta =-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\theta =-\frac{3\pi }{4}.
$$

Therefore, in order to find $Av$, we need to rotate $v$ clockwise by an angle of $\frac{3\pi }{4}$  and scale the result by a scale factor of $\frac{1}{2},$ as shown below.
